_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.holes is what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the machine is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: HP
entries.codex: A foe's health. What gets past its armour takes HP off, and at zero the foe falls. A machine's health is its hull.

design.holes: A machine's health is its hull; the engine's code may say either word.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage hits shield before hull. A shield absorbs its number: a blow costs it its damage, and whatever it cannot absorb passes to the hull, armour coming off it there. Nothing mends a shield by itself: a reboot brings it back whole, and a component, a module or a passive may add to one that still stands, up to the chassis maximum. A shield at nothing is Broken, and takes none until its machine reboots. The shield is full as every fight opens, as the heat starts at zero; nothing returns on the map.

design.holes: Rates and shield sizes are placeholders. No in-combat trickle; a passive may bring one back for one chassis.

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: A component that prints heat adds it when spent, and it stays: nothing cools a machine by itself. Heat may pass the chassis maximum, and what stands past it is Overheated: at the end of your turn, before the enemy acts, it burns hull one for one, every turn it stands there, and the first such turn since the machine's last reboot breaks its shield. A reboot takes the heat to nothing; a vent, a module or a passive that cools takes some off, what stands past the maximum first. A machine the burn wrecks is lost on its own turn. Foes never add heat: a Scorched machine's weapons and equipment aimed at foes run hotter for the turn.

design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow. Cooling numbers are placeholders; cooling must stay below a typical weapon's heat or heat never matters, and a vent component must be worth a whole turn (tuning).

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Two rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent die. A reroll lands on any other component on the die, never the one showing; a second copy of the same component may come up. Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds, unless a Giant Petrel fights: its Maverick's Playbook banks up to three left unspent as your turn ends, for the next round.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase, never inside a fight. It fills at the ramp's beat (3 turns, 2 from Convergence 8), a turn short of its peak as a battle opens, and the beat halves once at the Rupture. When full it resets and peaks: the rift sends the next composition of its cycle, every tear open before the peak sends a patrol, the seam creeps toward the gate, and new tears open on it. It never stops: the boss's seal breaking does not quiet it.

design.holes: The interval step inside a battle (the escalation a stall would meet) is on the ramp's table at zero until the turtle read asks for it.

entries.name: Rupture meter
entries.codex: Fills by the menace of the packs you kill, in any fight however it ends, toward the tier's Fractures (three, four or five), each later one costing more. The last, the Rupture, takes the packs the field opens with and the rift's first two peaks send, one lone patrol left over, and 4 more for each elite the tier's Fractures bring. The Rupture breaks the boss's seal, and nothing else does: a cleared field is breathing room until the next peak.

design.holes: Shown as a bar under the gate's with a notch a Fracture, a first cut; the beats, the patrol left and the steps are placeholders.

entries.name: Fracture
entries.codex: A step of the Rupture meter, paid out as a fight ends. At the Fractures the tier names (tier one's first; tier two's first and third; tier three's first, second and fourth) an elite emerges at the rift, the lead domain's elites in turn and never twice in a battle. The last Fracture is the Rupture.

design.holes: The prize a Fracture may bring is not built (decided after the meter is played); the Peak has no elite yet, so its Fractures send none.

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: Each pusher makes for a segment of the wall of its own, drawn as it is dealt. A pusher that ends its walk beside any hex of the gate or the wall strikes the gate's bar every turn: ten for each machine it is a fight for, less as it loses foes, at least one. The whole wall is the target, so no line plugs it. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.holes: The gate damage formula is a placeholder; city defences along the wall are not built.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.codex: A component that deals damage: spent on a foe within its reach, it deals its number in damage, then its keywords act and its heat lands. One that deals none is equipment.

design.holes: The engine's kind is attack for a weapon and a debuff alike: a debuff is an attack of no damage (Face.is_debuff), so code asks is_weapon() for this word and is_attack() for both.

entries.name: Shield component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that machine's shield maximum.

entries.name: Vent component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.codex: A buff or a debuff: a component that deals no damage. A buff is spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as it says) and grants it a status; a debuff is spent on a foe within its reach, its keywords its whole effect. Shields and vents are kinds of their own.

entries.name: Buff component
entries.codex: Equipment spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as the component says) that grants it a status, so many stacks deep, through the end of so many rounds: Empowered for damage, Armoured against damage, Primed to lay Ablating on hit. A status that runs down on its own (Empowered, halving) takes no rounds. The die shows the status name and the stacks.

entries.name: Direct
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any foe in either rank, at no cost to its firer.

entries.name: Spread
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Spread 2 also hits the foes beside the target in its rank, each taking 2 where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 2 as on the blow, then each foe's own statuses and armour. On a debuff it carries no number: its effects reach those foes, and it deals nothing.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (cleave), and the validator asks for it on a weapon. The half it dealt from 26 October retired 28 October (Ryan): at single digits a neighbour's half killed no rank and file. A piece may carry it beside Penetrate, the plus round its target; Splash, the two under one word, was cut on 15 November (Ryan: "It might be a more interesting game with only the other area shapes, with a few select pieces carrying both spread and penetrate together").

entries.name: Penetrate
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Penetrate 3 also hits the other rank of the target's column, which takes 3 where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 3 as on the blow, then the foe's own statuses and armour. A massive foe fills its column, so it is hit once. On a debuff it carries no number.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (penetrate), and the validator asks for it on a weapon.

entries.name: Every Foe
entries.codex: Targeting mode. Dropped on any foe, the entry lands on every foe in the fight, front rank and back, and none is its one target: a debuff's effects on each, or a weapon's strike on each for its whole number, so a Shock on any of them is doubled and spent..

design.holes: A keyword from 2 November (Ryan: 'Every foe is a targeting mode, just like spread, penetrate, and splash, it should be listed as such and given a keyword'), a targeting mode in its own right since 4 November ('Silence should not narrow targeting modes, that's why I'm switching them to targeting modes'), drawn in the die's targeting slot. A working name, the foes' Every Machine mirrored. A weapon's too since 12 November, when Sweep went (Ryan: the Whip Scorpion's and the Musk Ox's specials "a 'target all'"): it strikes every foe for its whole number and none is its one target (Ryan, 12 November: "Target all shouldn't need a target in the same way that sweep didn't. Why would only the first target pop shock? That's weird and useless"), so a Shock is doubled and spent on each and, with no primary target, no Ricochet follows it. No area keyword rides it.

entries.name: Every Ally
entries.codex: Targeting mode, a shield's or a buff's. Spent on any machine, the entry lands on the whole team, its own machine among them, each taking all of it..

design.holes: Every Foe's mirror on the team's side (2 November; a targeting mode since 4 November); a working name. Its mark is the three hexes under a low arch, its own cell lit (Ryan, 4 November: 'the difference is whether the center one is lit or not, its two modes, even if the every ally doesn't actually exist in game, yet'): no piece carries it yet. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Every Other Ally
entries.codex: Targeting mode, a shield's or a buff's. Spent on an ally, the entry lands on every machine but its own, each taking all of it..

design.holes: Every Ally's other mode (4 November), the Mooring Screens' team shield; a working name. Its mark is Every Ally's with its own cell dark. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Every foe the entry reaches gains that many stacks of Cryo a strike (Cryo 1: one stack), laid once the strikes are done, so a fire never cashes its own frost. Any machine's hit with a weapon on a foe carrying Cryo spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack.

design.holes: Other pieces may lay it (marked for reuse as a healthier ally cooling than a vent). A rider on the mark is benched until the roster has room. The cooling a stack is a placeholder.

entries.name: Ablate
entries.codex: Keyword with a number, the same on either side. On a weapon or equipment, Ablate 3 means each foe hit gains three stacks of Ablating. On a foe's attack, each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Ablating on the machine it hit.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (ablate), and the validator asks for it. Burn until 15 November: the word is Ryan's, for an eroding that is not only fire ("Ablating or ablate is very clinical, it fits the military notation, and evokes eating though armour to me"). A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Lure
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe, a weapon or equipment. Every foe the entry reaches turns on this machine for the round, a felled one too, intents and all; reach and area decide who and how many. A lured foe whose move has no target keeps doing it.

design.holes: No status and no chip: the arrow is the record. A draw by an ally is parked (the bible's redirection row).

entries.name: Shock
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. Every foe the entry reaches is Shocked, a felled one too: the next weapon strike aimed at it deals double. The entry's own blow never spends the shock it leaves.

entries.name: Expose
entries.codex: Keyword, on either side. On an entry of ours aimed at a foe: every foe the entry reaches is Exposed through your next turn, a felled one too: in Direct reach of every machine, and its armour counts for nothing. A second Expose refreshes it, never adds. On a foe's move, a rider on its blow or a move of its own: the machine it lands on is Exposed through the round after, its armour counting for nothing, and as that round opens every foe's targeted move turns on it, up to the blows that would wreck it. A Lure turns the move and a Ward turns it away; no foe announces one while another's is out or a machine stands Exposed.

design.holes: The formation word exposed stays rules text, so the status's id is exposure. The foes' half is Ryan's of 15 November (the vocabulary pass's fourth and fifth rounds), built 16 November: a tier-two foe's at the least, the validator refusing it on anything dealt at tier one ("only in formations that feel thematic and fair, so that the player has tools to answer by that point"), and one out at a time ("Enemy units should be smart enough to only try to Expose one player unit at a time"). No foe carries it yet: its carriers are the foes' pass's content. The foes' text is a session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Disrupt
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. The foe does its other move instead, this round, and its new intent shows at once. A foe with nothing else open is not moved, and a follow-up it announced is not either: the move it came after was the window.

design.holes: Deterministic: the next move in the foe's list that its conditions allow, so a boss steps through its pattern.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: Player keyword. The target skips its telegraphed action this round, and recovers with its stun resist in Numbed. On a Numbed foe the stun strips a stack and lands nothing; a Ward turns it away.

entries.name: Swap
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Dingo's Combat Translocator, a debuff): the spend takes two targets, a foe and then another foe or an empty slot, and the two trade places; no damage. A massive foe does not move. Drag the die to the first, drop it, then tap the second; drag it again to move it, or tap the ground to set it back.

design.holes: A keyword until 15 November (Ryan: "Can be unique text, not a keyworded rider"): the piece's own rule, `swaps` on its entry, its mark kept on the die.

entries.name: Brittle
entries.codex: Keyword with a number, the same on either side. On a weapon or equipment, Brittle 2 means each foe hit gains two stacks of Brittle a strike, laid once the strikes are done, so no strike of the spend feeds on what it lays. On a foe's attack, each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Brittle on the machine it hit; a Ward turns it away.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (brittle), and the validator asks for it. Flak on our side and Crush on the foes' until 15 November, one word on both since (Ryan: "Crushed and flak - agreed, brittle"). The word names the state, so a piece that lays it reads Brittle 2 and the Flak pieces keep their names; a verb for it is his to pick if he wants one. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Sap
entries.codex: Sap N: each foe hit gains N stacks of Sapped a strike, laid once the strikes are done, so no strike of the spend feeds on what it lays.

design.holes: The keyword that lays Ryan's Sapped (11 November), first on the Baboon's Redshift Emitter.

entries.name: Juggernaut Drive
entries.codex: Machine status, the Wild Boar's passive waiting. Its next weapon attack ignores armour, and that attack lifts it; equipment leaves it standing. Gained with a Barrier; one at a time. A purge takes it.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "After gaining Barrier, its next weapon attack gains Breach. The next attack breach will need to be represented by a purgeable buff, I'd just call it 'Juggernaut Breach.'" 15 November, Breach cut on our side: 'Change to explicit "ignores armour."', so the state shows under the passive's own name and the word Breach is gone from the game.

table.stacks: No: one, whatever grants it
table.lasts: Until its next weapon attack

entries.name: Numbed
entries.codex: Foe buff: the rounds until one stun lands. A stun on it strips a stack and lands nothing, so a foe with Numbed N takes N+1 stuns in a round. A stunned foe gains its stun resist in stacks (1 for most, 2 for a massive foe, 3 for an elite, a hero or a boss) as the turn it lost ends; a stack goes as each of its turns ends after that. A Purge lowers it like any buff; nothing deepens, spreads or cleanses it.

design.holes: Ryan's clock (2 November): the chip reads as the rounds until it can be stunned again, so the stacks land after the decay phase; a stun lock costs its resist and one every round, so an all-in stun team can brute-force a boss at a price, and a Purge is the other key. The resist numbers are placeholders (content's resist; the bosses' by hand).

table.stacks: Yes: its stun resist as it recovers from a stun
table.lasts: A stack goes as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Paradox
entries.codex: Foe status. While a machine runs the Paradox meter (the Baboon's Pocket Paradox), a foe gains a stack of Paradox for every stack of another debuff it gains; a debuff that never stacks, as Shocked or Suppressed, is one. At the machine's count (five) or more its past self knocks it out: every stack is consumed and it is Suppressed.

design.holes: The count is a placeholder (Ryan, 11 November: "we have no idea how many paradox stacks is balanced, we just decided on 3 or whatever as a placeholder without knowing how much status chips were going to get thrown around in the game as a whole"); a stack a debuff stack since that day, at five.

table.stacks: Yes: one for every debuff stack gained; at five or more it Suppresses and clears
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Volatile
entries.codex: A cost printed on any kind of component, along its foot beside its heat, the hull's mark (a machine's body) and a number. Volatile 3 means spending it costs its owner 3 hull, past shield and armour, before the component acts, and a machine it leaves at nothing is wrecked. A blank is never spent, so a jammed entry costs nothing.

design.holes: Hull outright, where the Corrupted bite takes shield first. The number is a placeholder. A keyword with a chip until 26 October; a cost like heat since, so the die says the price and no chip does.

entries.name: Shield cost
entries.codex: A cost printed on any kind of component, along its foot beside its heat, the shield's mark and a number: spending it takes that much shield from its owner first, overshield included. Short of it, the entry cannot be played: the die shows the cost struck through, and it has nowhere to land.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 26 October: a price paid in the buffer, which overshield cheats out at the cost of two actions for one effect; the first entry with a condition on its play, so advanced pieces may follow.
design.holes: No piece carries it yet; the numbers are content's.

entries.name: Targets
entries.codex: Whom a shield, a vent or a buff may be spent on: any ally or itself (the default), itself only, any other ally, or every machine at once: the whole team (Every Ally) or every machine but its own (Every Other Ally). On the die three connected hexes stand under its main mark, the middle its own machine and the two beside it its allies, a filled one a machine it may be spent on: all three for either, the middle alone for itself only, the two beside it for allies only.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: Keyword with a number, a weapon's. Chain 2 also lands 2 on every other Shocked foe on the field, wherever it stands, where the target takes the number: the attacker's bonuses land on that 2 as on the blow, then each foe's own statuses and armour. No strike is aimed at them, so their Shock stands.

design.holes: Shock's other payoff (Ryan, 28 October: 'the thinking man's AoE'); the kill and repeat and the ping retired; 29 October, Ryan's pick from six looks measured that day: its arcs plain and never spending a charge, with Shock read by a weapon's strike aimed at the foe alone, and a random charge after the arcs, since the arc was short of charges to find. Its number rides on the entry (chain). Retired 3 November: the charge, one other foe at random after the arcs (Ryan, 2 November: "Chain just is the situational aoe, and if weak we can either add more things for it to proc on, or give it the self-charge again"); Charged, the primer, supplies the Shock beside the Shock weapons and Retaliate.

entries.name: Rapid
entries.codex: After this component is spent the machine acts again: the die rerolls for free onto any other component (a second copy of this one included, so copies chain), and the entry spent stays dark for the rest of the round, its own cooldown, never printed, so each copy acts once a round. Any component may carry it, a vent or a shield as well as a weapon.

design.holes: Its limiter is its own switch-off, the entry dark for the rest of the round (Ryan, 12 November: "rapid gets its innate cooldown zero back without the explicit display"), which no cleanse lifts; a Rapid vent is never below tier three and a Rapid shield never below tier two (the bible's Rapid row).

entries.name: Instant
entries.codex: After this component is spent the machine acts again: the die rolls again for free and may land on this one again, so the same component can be spent again. On the Cassowary's die the roll spins the whole cylinder. Nothing goes dark: what it costs and the odds are its limit. Any component may carry it.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "the rapid no cooldown pieces change to a new keyword: Instant (reroll after use, can land on itself)". Every Instant piece carries a limiter, which the validator holds content to: a cooldown, heat, Volatile or a shield cost, or the store a charged form spends (the Knuckle of Fury's five rage); a piece locked on a stepping die has the cylinder's odds (the Spin-Up's). An entry is Rapid or Instant, never both.

entries.name: Jam
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The component the target's die is showing is Jammed through the target's next turn: if the die lands on it, it comes up blank.

design.holes: Disable until 15 November (Ryan: "Rename to Jammed"); the rider follows the pattern, Jam lays Jammed.

entries.name: Destroy
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. If any of the blow reaches the hull, the component the target's die is showing is destroyed: blank for the rest of the battle, and after it a hardpoint's is gone for good and a built-in one is rebuilt. A shield that takes the whole blow, a Barrier or a Ward keeps it, and a blank or a broken entry showing has nothing left to break.

design.holes: No foe carries it (Ryan, 15 November: "This can be a boss-level rider, that destroys the visible face if it damages hull at all. Only promoted form or superboss-level so we're not tuning the economy around it. No longer a general rule"). Its carrier is the foes' pass's, and the fight bot prices no entry's loss until one does.

entries.name: Drain
entries.codex: Ability, the Vampire Lord's own: every blow it lands heals it by what the blow took from the hull, no more than the machine had, so a shield starves it. It lays nothing on the machine, so no Ward turns it away; a Barrier's blow deals nothing to drain, and Ablating on the foe takes back what it heals. No Purge reaches it.

design.holes: The Vampire Lord's (30 October), its bite and, below half, a drain at every machine. The genre's word (Drain), and the soft counter section 2 asks for: Ablating never stops healing. The hull alone, so the shield answers it: a drain of shield and hull walled the slowest trio at every HP tried, the shield, its answer to every blow, doing nothing against the heal. A rider on its blows until 16 November, and the unit's own Ability since, on Ryan's mark of 15 November ("This should be moved to an ability on the unit since it's on every attack. Like the Nob"): a chip on the foe, every blow of its, and no word on the blow. The text is a session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Corrupt
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Corrupted on the component the target's die is showing (Corrupt 2: two): it deals damage to its owner whenever spent, a bite a stack.

entries.name: Swallow
entries.codex: Foe move of its own, never a rider on a blow. The machine it lands on is Swallowed: out of the fight for the rounds it says, until the swallower falls, or until the swallower has lost a quarter of its HP since the swallow, the damage still to deal counting down on its chip. It never takes the last machine able to act. A Ward turns it away; a Lure turns it, and a Suppress or a Disrupt stops it, as any move.

design.holes: Floraison's (30 October). The rounds, 1 to 3, are the move's, and no damage lands on the machine while it is held. The early release (31 October, Ryan agreeing Claude's lean): a quarter of the swallower's HP lost since the swallow, Clair Obscur's stagger in its smallest form, a round of the team's focus; the swallower loses nothing else, since a lost action on top would be a stun. A machine let go in the player's turn acts that round.

entries.name: Golden Rage
entries.codex: Foe move of its own, never a rider on a blow: the foe goes gold (Golden) for the rounds it says, so the round it roars is the window to shield up or to start the burst. It goes gold only while calm, so one rage at a time; a Suppress or a Disrupt stops the roar, as any move.

design.holes: The Thunder Ape's (4 November); see Golden. Its weight is content's, 2 so it comes about a round in three while calm.

entries.name: Merge
entries.codex: Foe move of its own. Every other foe on the field of the kinds it names is taken into it, gone without falling: it regrows the HP they had left, and its next move hits harder for each one. Thin them first; a Suppress or a Disrupt stops it, as any move.

design.holes: The King Gel's (30 October): every Gel, Bubble Gel, Metal Gel and half on the field. Content: effect merge, foe (an id or a list), value (the lift a foe taken in). A foe taken in leaves no last act and no split and is no kill of the team's; its pack's tally still counts it gone. It needs its kinds beside it, so the King Gel's escort is its own (an escort that names its boss).

entries.name: Purge
entries.codex: Purge N, on either side. On a player's entry aimed at a foe, a weapon or equipment, every foe it reaches loses N stacks of every buff it carries (an unstackable one is a stack of one), after the blow, so a foe the blow kills stays down. On a foe's move of its own, never a rider on a blow and never a last act's, the machine it lands on loses N stacks of every buff it carries, for good. A stack is a stack, whatever granted it; an Ability is no buff and stays, and so do the stores. A Ward turns it away and stands, on either side.

design.holes: One id, dispel, on both sides (28 October); numbered 2 November (Ryan: "lower everything by N and price accordingly", a softer answer to armour and damage stacking that prices cheap and common; the Null Field Emitter at Purge 2, a placeholder). One purge on either side (Effects.purge): N stacks off every buff, whatever granted it (Ryan, 8 November: "A stack is a stack, doesn't matter where it came from"); retired with it the purge by source of 28 October (a die entry's stacks gone for good, a store's, a form's or a passive's put to sleep until the player's turn), which he called cryptic. What the unit is, its form or its passive mechanic, is an Ability and no buff, so no purge reaches it (the same day).

entries.name: Cleanse
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield and vent components. Whoever the component is spent on also loses every Ablating, Scorched, Brittle, Jammed and Corrupted status. A rapid component's own switch-off is not a status a cleanse touches. On a foe's move of its own, the same word: every mark the team laid (Ablating, Brittle, Cryo, Vitriol, Shocked, Exposed, the Web Bomb, the Paradox, the Drone) comes off the most-marked of its own, never Numbed or Suppressed.

entries.name: Retaliate
entries.codex: Machine status. While it lasts, a foe that strikes this machine's bare hull is Shocked. It lasts the rounds the component that grants it says.

design.holes: Cut as a buff word on 15 November (Ryan's mark on the vocabulary's table), its rule out of the engine. Kept as a planned draft, never shown, so the Retribution Thurible, back in design the same day ("It can have unique text but not until we sort out our fundamentals"), and two foes' planned moves still read: when the Thurible comes back its rule is its own text, and this entry goes.

table.stacks: No: one does all it does
table.lasts: The buff's rounds

entries.name: Shocked
entries.codex: Foe status. When a weapon's strike aimed at this foe lands, it deals double damage and the status clears. A blow that only reaches it (an area, a Chain's arc, a spill) neither doubles nor clears it, and equipment (a lure, a probe) leaves it standing. Never stacks. Laid by the Shock keyword, by a Charged machine's weapon, and on a foe that strikes the bare hull of a machine carrying Retaliate.

table.stacks: Never
table.lasts: Until the next team blow of a weapon

entries.name: Pinned
entries.codex: Foe status, from the Hollow-point Harpoon. The next time its Brittle would halve, it does not, and the pin is spent. Refreshed, never added.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "The Flak pin should be its own status that gets applied for one turn. I assume we're going to want a similar one for burning as well." Pinned Flak until 15 November, and what it holds Brittle since; the name is his ("Just \"Pinned.\"").

table.stacks: Never: a second pin refreshes it
table.lasts: Until the halving it stops

entries.name: Seared
entries.codex: Foe status. The next time its Ablating would lose a stack, it takes its points and loses none, and the pin is spent. Refreshed, never added.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: coded in beside Brittle's pin, "since the Mastema will want it as a fitted piece, if nothing else". No piece lays it yet. The name is his, 15 November: "Rename 'Seared.'"

table.stacks: Never: a second pin refreshes it
table.lasts: Until the fade it stops

entries.name: Sapped
entries.codex: Status, on a foe or a machine. Its attacks deal 1 less damage a stack, never below nothing. Every stack goes after its next turn: a foe's after its next action, a machine's after your next turn. A foe's Ward turns it away; a Cleanse clears it from a machine.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "I'd like to code in Weaken ... Weaken (debuff): Deals 1 less damage per stack with attacks ... Weaken can apply to both sides, it's not a bad soft CC from the foes to apply"; then "Weaken can change till after it's next turn then, instead of round end. Let's use Sapped." So a foe's Sapped laid in its turn reaches the machine's next attack.

table.stacks: Yes: every Sap adds
table.lasts: Until after its next turn

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: Status, on either side: its armour counts for nothing, its own and any Armoured. On a foe: in Direct reach of every machine as if its column's front were empty, through your next turn, falling as the foes' turn starts in the round after it landed; refreshed, never added. On a machine, from a foe's Expose: through the round after it lands, and as that round opens every foe's targeted move turns on it, whatever the foe's aim, until the blows already drawn would wreck it, the rest picking as they would. Armour it gains while Exposed does nothing until the mark ends; its shield is untouched. A Lure pulls a blow off it, and a Cleanse gives the armour back and leaves the intents where they turned.

design.holes: The id is exposure, since exposed names the formation word and the foes' default aim; a machine's is exposure_mech in the engine. The machine's half is Ryan's of 15 November, built 16 November: "all armour of all kinds"; "Exposed does not strip the petrel's resistant shield"; "keep the logic where enemies don't try and overkill. That helps keep it fair. So the whole field targets up until predicted death, then the rest pick intent targets as normal"; "Exposed sets the intents, everything after proceeds as normal"; "Lure wins". A session's reads where his words give none: a countdown's pick carried from the round before holds, and a machine out of reach (Phased as the round ended) draws nothing. Still his: whether a machine that stands Exposed may be marked again; built as no, so the whole field's fire comes every other round at most. The aim content calls exposed, shown as "aims at the exposed", is no mark and wants another word, his. The machine's text is a session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: Never: a second Expose refreshes it
table.lasts: A foe's through the player's next turn, falling as its turn starts; a machine's through the round after it lands

entries.name: Empowered
entries.codex: Machine status. Each stack is +1 damage on this machine's attacks, flat, so the count is the bonus. As its turn ends it halves, rounded down, whatever granted it, until it is gone.

design.holes: Every grant is one status on the machine and the stacks add up. A halving rule has no duration, so a buff component grants stacks and no rounds. The name is a placeholder. It halves at END TURN since 16 November (Ryan: "Empowered should decay at the end of turn, clearly, not end of round"), so what a machine gains in the enemy's turn it carries whole into its next; at the round's end until then.

table.stacks: Yes: a damage point a stack
table.lasts: Halves as its turn ends, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Sealed
entries.codex: Ability, the Polar Bear's form. Equipment it spends on itself seals it: armour up by its Lockdown's number, its own cooling stopped, its Cryo Flinger gaining Spread, and it runs hotter at the end of each turn. A weapon it fires opens it; equipment on an ally and a debuff, its lure among them, leave it as it is. No Purge touches it.

design.holes: One chip, renewing, never stacking: the armour it grants is tied to the form. The numbers are placeholders.

table.stacks: Renews: one seal however often it seals
table.lasts: Until a weapon it fires opens it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Changed Over
entries.codex: Ability, the Clydesdale's batteries. Its second battery is up and its first stowed, so its die rolls the second battery and its Changeover; with no chip, the first battery is up. It stays from fight to fight through a battle, and no Purge touches it.

design.holes: A working name and text, Claude's drafts of 11 November for Ryan to rewrite. One chip for the second battery, none for the first.

table.stacks: Renews: one chip
table.lasts: Until the Changeover turns the die back, or the battle ends

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Foe status, the mark the Cryo keyword leaves. Any machine's hit on it with a weapon spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack; equipment spends none. It never fades on its own.

design.holes: Engine id cryoed, since the keyword holds cryo; the player reads Cryo on both.

table.stacks: Yes: the Cryo's number per foe reached; a weapon's hit spends every stack
table.lasts: Until a weapon's hit spends it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Armoured
entries.codex: Status, on either side. Armour +1 a stack: that much off every blow that reaches it, flat, every stack at once, whatever granted it, so the count is the armour. It lasts until its next turn starts: a machine's (a buff, an armouring component, a passive) through the enemy's turn, coming off blows on bare hull, and a foe's, from its brace or another's, through the player's.

design.holes: The engine id stays braced. One clock on both sides, the opening of its side's next turn (Ryan, 15 November: "The common "end" state between both sides is "start of their next turn.""; 16 November, of a machine's, which went at the round's end until then: "Armoured we should change so its end is symmetrical on both sides. Probably means until "start of its next turn.""). A machine's goes as the round opens, before the foes announce, so no blow lands between its old end and its new one. It takes no rounds from any grant.

table.stacks: Yes: an armour point a stack, every stack going at once
table.lasts: Until its next turn starts

entries.name: Primed
entries.codex: Status, on either side: a stack a weapon fired, each lending Ablate 1. While a machine carries it its weapons fire with Ablate 1, a stack of Ablating a strike on each foe hit, one more than its own on a gun that carries Ablate, shown on the die and laid after the hits; a weapon fired spends a stack, equipment carries it not and spends nothing, and a Purge lowers it. On a foe, a stoker's move primes every other foe on the field, its value in stacks: each blow of a move that strikes leaves Ablating 1 on the machine it hits and that move spends a stack, a move that strikes nobody spending none. A machine's Ward turns the Ablating away, as it does any rider.

design.holes: The third primer since 15 November, beside Charged and Supercooled (Ryan: "give it the same format as cryo ... use a stack on firing"; "Primed - agreed, how many Ablate stacks does each Primed stack apply? Just one, like supercooled?"; one, since Ablate 1 on a gun measures as about the point a Charged stack's Shock does). Until then every blow left a stack of Ablating a stack of Primed, for a buff's rounds on a machine and one move on a foe. A placeholder name.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack a weapon fired, each lending Ablate 1
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Jammed
entries.codex: Component status. This die entry comes up blank while it lasts; the component itself is untouched. A foe's jam lasts through the machine's next turn and can be cleansed; a rapid component's own switch-off ends with the round, and is no jam.

design.holes: Disabled until 15 November (Ryan: "Rename to Jammed"). The engine's own name for an entry switched off, by a jam or by a cooldown, stays disabled.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the machine's next turn ends

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.codex: Component status. Every time this die entry is spent it bites its owner for 3 per stack, shield first, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a jammed entry does not bite. Stacks. Clears at end of skirmish. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: The bite is the status's own number in the engine's table, a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: its bite a stack
table.lasts: The skirmish

entries.name: Phased
entries.codex: Machine status. It cannot be damaged or targeted by anything until the end of the round, by either side, and it acts: no foe picks it, a blow or a move at every machine passes it by, no ally may spend on it, and nothing of its own damages it either, its heat past the maximum or a Volatile bite. Everything it carries ticks all the same, so a debuff runs down while it waits; the heat stays, and burns the turn it is back in reach. It is granted at the end of the round, to a machine that still stands, so it is queued a round ahead and lasts the whole of the next.

design.holes: Ryan's mark, 15 November: "New effect: "Cannot be damaged or targeted by anything until the end of this round." We remove the awkward act clause, but still ensure that it cannot be buffed or interacted with by allies until it unphases"; "all sources of Phased should say "at the end of this round, grant Phased.""; and his answer: "it's a safe reboot if you can pull it off. All phased granters need to be gated, it should be earned, with the caveat that you have to survive the current round". Engine ids phased and phasing, the wait a source lays, a buff a Purge takes. Its own heat does not burn it (his ruling, 16 November, on a session's read that had the burn land: "it shouldn't take damage from overheating since we don't need the exception. It does accumulate the stacks, though, which it will feel the round after"). Everything it carries ticks (16 November: "Everything ticks during phased. It doesn't take damage but it's a way of waiting out a debuff. That's why my clause of the self-cleanse and self-purge is our way out if it's broken"), so its Ablating fades a stack a turn and takes nothing, and its Regenerating runs. A Volatile bite and a corrupted entry's bite are blocked with the rest ("I think we block the damage as a feature, and see how bad it is once we have real hull cost pieces that matter"). A session's reads of his words: it may spend on itself, and its Lure turns no pick. His spare clause is held until play asks for it ("If that's too strong, I would add "Remove all buffs and debuffs. Cannot gain any buffs or debuffs while Phased.""). A foe's Phased is allowed and not built, the foes' pass's ("Phased on foes can be less strict since it's balanced around their kit and theme"). Until 15 November: cannot act, take damage or be targeted until the round's end, granted at once to a machine yet to act. A session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Granted as the round ends, to a machine that stands; until the next round's end

entries.name: Ablating
entries.codex: Status, the same on either side: it takes a point a stack, then loses a stack. On a foe: its HP, past armour, as its turn ends, so a burning foe strikes before it burns. On a machine: its shield first, then its hull past armour, at the end of the player's turn, before the overheat, so a Cleanse that turn takes it off. A tick is no blow: a Barrier neither stops it nor is spent on it.

design.holes: Engine ids ablating (a foe's) and ablating_mech (a machine's). Ryan's rule, 15 November, in the place of Burning as heat on a machine: "hits shield first, I think. Pretty deadly otherwise. Bypasses armour when damaging hull"; "Tick of ablate ignores barrier yes". A Phased machine takes no point and its stack fades all the same, and a Swallowed one's stacks wait (Ryan, 16 November: "Everything ticks during phased. It doesn't take damage but it's a way of waiting out a debuff"; "Swallowed it's out of play so everything should pause"). The foes' numbers are still the ones sized as heat, his to set. A session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: Yes: the Ablate's number per blow, or as many as the foe's move says
table.lasts: Until the stacks run out: one fades at each tick, as its turn ends (a foe's own action done; the end of the player's turn on a machine)

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex: Foe status. Skips its next turn, and is spent with it.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: One turn: this round's, or the next if it has acted

entries.name: Vitriol
entries.codex: Foe status, the funnel-web's acid. As its turn ends it loses 10% of its current HP a stack, past armour, after Ablating, rounded down, then a stack fades. A share of what is left: it opens on a boss and never finishes a foe.

design.holes: Only the funnel-web's passive lays it; a keyword that ever carries it shares the word. Whether a tick passes Guarded is the parts' question, as Ablating's is. The word Corroded is kept for a foe's damage over time on machines.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack per weapon hit on a foe showing no intent on the spider; a tick a stack
table.lasts: A stack fades as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Web Bomb
entries.codex: Foe status, the mark the Funnel-web's Web Bomb leaves on the foe it hits, the piece's own rule. As the round ends the web bursts: it and the foe beside it are Suppressed, each losing its next turn, each a stun like any other (a Numbed foe strips a stack instead, a Warded one turns it). Every foe still acts in the round the web is laid. Felled before the round ends, it takes its web with it; one the team has stunned this round has just gained its Numbed, so the burst strips a stack of that and stuns nothing.

design.holes: The burst catches the next foe to act beside it in its rank, the one to its left when none stands to its right; on a foe already suppressed it is wasted, and each half feeds the Paradox as the Suppress keyword's does. Named for its piece and its rider no keyword since 15 November (Ryan: "I don't think the rider needs to be listed as a keyword. It's a unique effect, and the debuff can be renamed \"web bomb.\""); the id is the engine's.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the round's end, when it bursts

entries.name: Spun Up
entries.codex: Machine status, the Cassowary's. The next weapon it spends deals 2 more a stack and takes every stack; equipment leaves them standing. Carried between turns until then.

design.holes: Spent whole by the next weapon, equipment leaving it: weapon only until balance says otherwise (Ryan, 26 October).

table.stacks: Yes: its bonus a stack, every stack spent by the next weapon
table.lasts: Until the next weapon it spends, across turns

entries.name: Ricochet
entries.codex: Machine status, the Skua's. After a weapon fires, it hits its target again for 1, once a stack, with every effect of the weapon but its area. Each is a strike of its own, so armour comes off it and a flat buff adds to it. Hull damage halves the stacks, rounded down. It lasts the fight.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "Ricochet (buff): After firing a weapon, it hits the primary target 1 more time per stack, dealing 1 damage each time and applying all effects other than area keywords"; "I'm leaving what applies in the ricochets open, if applying unique effects N more times is broken, then we dial it back and explicitly say 'keywords' instead of 'effects'"; 11 November: "Lose half stacks of Ricochet on any hull damage". His first thought, a Ricochet on every foe a weapon hits, he dropped with Sweep. Claude's readings, built on his go and his to move: 1 in place of the entry's number and of its reads of the foe, the firer's adds on it; half rounded down at each blow, bite or overheat that takes hull, so a lone stack is lost; no cap; a buff a Purge takes.

table.stacks: Yes: a strike of 1 more a stack after each shot
table.lasts: The fight; hull damage halves it

entries.name: Essence
entries.codex: Ability, the Ammit's. 1 Essence for every foe that falls in a fight it is in, whoever fells it, kept from fight to fight through the battle, with no limit. As each fight opens, and at the end of a round in which the Ammit killed, it gains 1 Empowered for every 5 Essence it holds; its Quintessence Tap consumes it. No Purge or Cleanse touches it.

design.holes: Ryan's rework of 12 November, Souls then; Essence his name of 15 November ("Rename souls to Essence"). No cap by his call ("as part of the fantasy"), so it is no store, which is capped and wears a bar: an Ability, a chip with its count. The kill's flare is once a round, as it ends, when an attack of the Ammit's killed in it (Ryan, 16 November: "at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy"); once an attack that killed from 12 November until then ("Flaring twice for an AoE is probably wrong, let's make it 'one of more killed' by an attack"), and once for each foe in the first build. The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: Yes: one for every foe that falls in its fight, with no cap
table.lasts: The battle

entries.name: Essence Flare
entries.codex: Machine status, from the Ammit's Quintessence Tap, on the machine that spent it. While it lasts no Empowered halves this round, its own or any other unit's, machine and foe alike: a machine's as the player's turn ends, a foe's as its own turn does. Until the round's end. A buff like any: a Purge takes it and the hold with it, and a wreck holds nothing.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "No Empowered decays this round. And I mean none, not ally or enemy." Pinned Empowered until 15 November, a chip on every unit holding Empowered and the round's own rule; then his: "This is not pinned empowered, this is an Ammit specific buff. I would give it to the Ammit only, even though it affects the whole battlefield"; "Grants the no-decay state which is represented as a buff on the Ammit called Essence Flare." That a Purge ends the hold follows from its being a buff.

table.stacks: Never: one, renewed
table.lasts: Until the round's end

entries.name: Shots
entries.codex: Machine count, the Cassowary's: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe this fight, shown as six pips under the heat bar, the sixth lit when it is next, where its sixth shot counts double. Shields, vents, buffs and spins are no shots. Never a chip; nothing cleanses it; it resets each fight.

design.holes: Kept only for a machine whose rule counts (an nth_shot condition).

table.stacks: Yes: one a weapon or equipment aimed at a foe
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Quick turn spent
entries.codex: Machine marker, the Needletail's: its die has turned once this round, so the spend it holds is its last. Never a chip: the die shows the turn it still has in its passive box. Gone at the round's end.

design.holes: Set by the static one_of_each (the Needletail's relay): two things a round, a weapon and an equipment.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: The round

entries.name: Brittle
entries.codex: Status, the same on either side: every blow its carrier takes deals a point more a stack, and the stacks halve as its turn starts, rounded down, the other side's blows behind it. On a foe: every blow of a weapon, one of 0 included, added before its armour comes off. On a machine: every blow a foe lands, the shield taking the extra first as it takes any blow; an ally's Cleanse lifts it.

design.holes: Engine ids brittled (a foe's) and brittled_mech (a machine's). Flak on a foe (Wainwright & Sutler's on-hit, 19 October) and Crushed on a machine (the World Eater's pin, 4 November, Monster Hunter's Defense Down by archetype; Ryan: "that inflicts Defense Down in game, something we don't have") until 15 November, folded on Ryan's mark ("We could consider making this one symmetrical and folding it into Flak as well, changing the name so it works on both sides") and his "agreed, brittle". One clock, the halving: a machine's stood whole through the next round until then, so a foe's Brittle 1 was the pack's for the turn it was laid in and gone by the next, and a foe lays 2 at the least since 16 November (Ryan: "Buffs and debuffs that decay at end of round should just have a minimum of 2"; the validator holds a foe's moves to it, and our own pieces are not held to it: "The minimum 2 is different for the player since they can sequence. So I wouldn't make it a blanket rule"). Adds before multiplies and before armour, to a weapon's blow of 0 too (Ryan, 25 October: "Flak and overcharge exist in part to get past armour"), so a Shocked foe carrying Brittle takes blow plus Brittle, doubled. Numbers are placeholders; Brittle beside Empowered at a point a stack each may read too strong, the two read together on the Prairie Dog's rows. A session's draft, his to write. It halves as its carrier's turn starts since 16 November (his four places, Brittle with what ends at a turn's start; at the round's end until then, no blow apart).

table.stacks: Yes: N a hit from a Brittle N piece, N a blow from a foe's Brittle N; a point more on every blow it takes, a stack
table.lasts: Halves as its turn starts, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex: Machine status. A destroyed component is blank: it does nothing when it comes up, and provides its passive bonuses but not passive abilities, for the rest of the battle; after it, a hardpoint's is gone for good and a built-in one is rebuilt. One thing destroys a component, a foe's blow that carries Destroy, when any of it reaches the hull, and it destroys the entry the die shows: one that lands on a destroyed component or an empty hardpoint finds nothing to break, so what faces the enemy is the player's choice. No blow destroys one by its size.

design.holes: No foe carries Destroy yet, so nothing is destroyed in play (Ryan, 15 November: "Only promoted form or superboss-level so we're not tuning the economy around it. No longer a general rule"). The campaign's hangar screen is not built.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Four slots, one a column. Front-rank foes fill these. Always in Direct reach.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Four slots behind the front. Back-rank foes hold these.

entries.name: Mine
entries.codex: Foe status, the Lammergeier's: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe adds its flat damage to a Mine on that foe, with what the spend fired at it: every hit's stacks and its other keywords, one Mine a foe however many spends feed it. When the foe falls, even one that gets back up or splits, the Mine blows: its damage on every foe round its slot, each through its own Brittle and armour, then its keywords as on a blow. Spread, Penetrate, a spill behind and Lure stay with the spend, and its damage never grows with the spend's. The chip shows its damage; its readout, its keywords.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "the lammergeier basically converts all hits to AoE hits, at the cost of a delay until Death". One Mine a spend at a flat 2 ("then look at per hit later if it's weak"); its riders the spend's whole result on the foe ("the mine should take the entire result of the spend, then apply it. So a 3-hit flak that burns 1 per hit if the target is under 50% HP, would result in adding a 2 damage mine with 3 flak, and 0-3 burn"), every hit's stacks as its machine deepened and doubled them and a gated keyword where its gate held ("if a gate is met when fired only, then apply it"); the numbered ones add up and the rest ride once; Chain rides as its arcs (Claude's lean, which he took); in the enemy's turn a Mine's Disrupt does nothing; a Suppress rides as fired, each foe the blast meets judging its own Numbed (Claude's read; Ryan: "Your reads are correct"). A mark the team laid: a Ward turns it away, a foe's cleanse takes it, the Paradox counts it. A foe taken into a merge hands its Mine to the merger.

table.stacks: Yes: its damage, every spend adding to it, one Mine a foe
table.lasts: The fight, until the foe falls or the Syrinx Drone detonates it

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.

design.holes: Spread treats it as a front-rank neighbour; Penetrate finds nothing behind it.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Move in hexes: how far a machine goes in an action, a step a hex. Water costs a ground machine two; a hovercraft and a flyer cross it at one; walls are the flyer's alone.

design.holes: Every chassis's move is a placeholder set by size and role; what crossing water and walls is worth is the pricing run's to read (28 October).

entries.name: Walk
entries.codex: The map shows where every pack will walk on the enemy's turn, worked out from where your machines stand now: a pusher toward the gate, a hunter toward its prey. Packs go round your machines; nothing you do stops one, and nothing a pack does reacts to your plan.

design.holes: A pack with no way to the gate waits, and the map says so.

entries.name: Fight
entries.codex: Tap a pack to attack it. One pack is one fight: nothing joins it, and you commit the machines beside it. Orders onto several packs play one fight at a time, each resolved before the next and fought to its end; a machine that fought, won or lost, is spent until your next turn.

entries.name: Spent
entries.codex: A machine that has fought this turn is spent: it cannot move or fight again until your next turn. A machine whose passive grants a second action has two before it is spent.

entries.name: Carry
entries.codex: A machine that carries (the Swallowtail's Muster Deck) lifts the machines on the hexes beside it when it moves: they travel as a ring round it and land as a block, each where it rode from it, keeping whatever move and action they had. It cannot stop where a rider would land on a hex it cannot stand on (NO ROOM). A caught machine does not ride.

design.holes: A landing animation or a redistribution on landing may come later.

entries.name: Caught
entries.codex: A machine a hunter has caught fights it first on your turn, before any other fight, and cannot move until then. Others in range may join that fight. It is fought to its end: the hunter falls or the machine is wrecked.

entries.name: Ring
entries.codex: A hunter catches what stands beside where its walk ends: the engage range, one hex, the same reach every unit has on the map, so a machine joins a fight on a pack beside it and a hunter catches a machine beside it. The map draws the ring of hexes beside the hunter's walk's end, where the catch is judged, and round the hunter while a catch it made waits. No other pack has a ring. No pack joins a fight; one pack is one fight.

design.holes: One number in the engine, the engage range (Unit.ENGAGE_RANGE, a placeholder: adjacency), serving the machines' reach onto a pack, the hunters' catch and the ring drawn; the hunters' pounce of two (Ryan, 29 October, "wolfs pounce") retired 10 November with the body blocking, so the catch is "the same melee engage range as everyone else" (Ryan); no foe or composition carries a ring since 8 November.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries.codex: A pack pushes unless its composition hunts. A pusher walks toward the gate and threatens nothing else. A hunter locks one machine, by its caveat (the nearest, weakest, strongest or slowest), puts its tag on it and walks toward it; when it ends its walk beside its prey it has caught it, and that fight comes first on your next turn. A caught machine cannot move until the fight, and is caught again while the hunter lives. A prey that keeps its distance is safe; one sealed off behind walls and machines is not: the hunter catches whichever machine it can reach that turn standing nearest it, and its tag moves there.

design.holes: Push and hunt are the only behaviours; the hunters' caveats are placeholders.

entries.name: Pack
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a pack: a composition on one hex, its members listed on a hold, wearing its lead's picture, hunting when its composition says so, walking at its slowest member's pace. Its hold says first how many machines it is a fight for, its threat rating; a pusher walks to a segment of the wall of its own. A fight is the one pack you attack. A boss is one unit on one hex.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: Every unit covers one hex, the boss included: it is occupied, counts for rings and range, and is a tap target. The gate and the rift are wider structures.

design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A pack that ends its walk beside a gate hex or a wall hex strikes the gate. A tear is a mouth, not a structure: its hex can be walked and stood on.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: At a peak of Rift Pressure the next composition of the rift's cycle (the tier's formations and patrols in turn, the lead domain's and the guest's in turn) emerges at the rift, and every tear open before the peak sends a patrol. A spawn lands on the nearest free hex to its mouth with no machine beside it, at the end of the enemy's turn, so you see it and its walk for a whole turn and nothing lands on top of a detachment.

entries.name: Composition
entries.codex: What the rift sends and what stands on the field when a battle starts: a patrol (a few foes, one machine's fight), a formation (the body's fight), an elite leading its own, or a boss's escort. A composition is one pack on one hex: its members, listed on a hold, unpack into the fight together and come back by member. Each domain writes its compositions by tier; the ramp sets how many stand at the start and how thick they are.

design.holes: Each tier's compositions are partitioned from its list as placeholders for Ryan's marks; no escort composition is written yet, so every boss brings the tier's units.

entries.name: Patrol
entries.codex: The small composition: a few foes, a fight for one machine, the threat rating its hold shows. Two stand on the flanks at the start (one from Convergence 8), and the tears send nothing else.

design.holes: The tier-one patrols read as a lone starter's fight on the greedy rung, not a tenth of its hull (docs/measurements.md, 30 October); their sizes are Ryan's to mark.

entries.name: Formation
entries.codex: The body's composition: a fight for three machines, the threat rating its hold shows. One stands on the field at the start (two from Convergence 3, three from 8), and the rift alone sends more, at its peaks. A domain's tier writes its formations; the lead's and the guest's come in turn.

design.holes: The word also names the skirmish's two ranks; the context tells them apart.

entries.name: Tear
entries.codex: A mouth beside the rift's. At a peak of Rift Pressure the ramp's count of tears (one; two from Convergence 8) open on the seam, a few rows past the rift (row 4 at twelve deep) and creeping toward the wall, as far from the rift and the other tears as the row allows, and every tear open before the peak sends a patrol. A tear opens a peak before it first sends, so where the next flood comes from is known an interval ahead. Tears stay open and never close.

design.holes: Drawn as a first cut for the phone; its mark and its opening are to judge running (RIFTGATE_PEAK_DEBUG=1 peaks every enemy turn).

entries.name: Seam
entries.codex: The flattening's edge: the row the rift's bleed reaches, a row for every five of the field's depth and one more at the start (row 4 at twelve deep), creeping two rows toward the gate at every peak, as far as the row before the wall. The tears open on it. It is the clock's picture: no rule reads the ground behind it.

design.holes: The creep a peak is a placeholder (the ramp's table, flat at two).

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Open ground. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Open ground, the same as plain: the road is art. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Forest and scrub. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Rubble. Every machine and pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet; what terrain does in a fight is section 12's question.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Tracks, walkers and wheels wade it, a hex costing two of their move; hovercraft and flyers cross it at full pace. Packs wade it as the ground machines do; a winged pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet (section 12). Each map shape lays its own water (a river with narrows and tributaries, the flooded fjord, ponds, a pond, the gorge's flooded channels, the city's flooded streets, or none). Since 29 October the horde wades it as the ground machines do, so water slows a crossing and never walls it; the crossing guarantee binds the walls.

entries.name: Crags
entries.codex: Rock spikes. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Mesas
entries.codex: Flat-topped rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Towers
entries.codex: Dead skyscrapers. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Cliffs
entries.codex: A wall of rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Crosses everything, water and walls included. It flies over machines and packs, and they pass under it, but nothing stops on another's hex.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Skims water at full pace; walls stop it.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Legs. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Tracked
entries.codex: Tracks. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Wheeled
entries.codex: Wheels. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A static player-side unit. Not on the field yet.

design.holes: No die and no rule yet: how gate defences work is section 12's question.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires on every attack, after its number is read. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, multiply the printed number alone before any buff (the Kite's double, on an unhurt foe), or set a minimum damage.

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains shield from any source, with the amount gained; it may shed heat or grant a status, never raise more shield.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On shielding an ally
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine spends a shield component on an ally, with the shield's size; it may shed the ally's heat or grant the ally a status, never raise more shield. It never fires for a shield on itself.

design.holes: Fires on the spend, whatever the shield gained, so a shield die on a topped-up ally still does its other work.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains heat, with the amount; it may raise shield or grant a status, never add heat.

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once as the skirmish begins, before the first roll: a shield, a vent, a status.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On foe status
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when any foe gains a status, whoever applied it: once for each status a spend puts on a foe, however many strikes or stacks (an application, not a stack). Never for Paradox, nor for the Suppressed a Paradox causes, and Numbed is no status. Effects: paradox (the foe gains a stack of Paradox; at the count it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears).

entries.name: On applying stacks
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine applies stacks of a status to anyone: a foe's Ablating (from an Ablate or from Primed), an ally's or its own buff, its own Empowered from a kill. Effects: add_stacks (so many stacks more, flat or for every so much heat the machine carries). Never for Numbed, which is exempt from every interaction.

design.holes: Shocked and Suppressed are not stacks, so it never touches them.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine loses hull: to a blow, a bite or an overheat.

design.holes: The hook for the pinned berserker idea too.

entries.name: On a hit on its shield
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when a foe's blow lands on this machine's shield and puts nothing on its hull; a blow that wounds fires On hull damage alone.

design.holes: The Nemesis's rage, one a hit on its shield (Ryan, 11 November: "hull damage takes priority").

entries.name: On a blow blocked
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once for every blow of this machine's weapons that a living foe's armour or Barrier takes whole, each foe's of an area and each strike's.

design.holes: The Nemesis's rage, two a blow blocked (Ryan, 11 November: per blow, "that lets it scrap against the comp its supposed to").

entries.name: On gaining a Barrier
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as this machine gains a Barrier, from its own equipment or an ally's.

design.holes: The Wild Boar's Juggernaut Drive (Ryan, 11 November: "After gaining Barrier, its next weapon attack gains Breach"; ignores armour since 15 November).

entries.name: On a kill
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once after an attack of this machine's that killed, however many foes fell to it, chains and spills included: a status, a shield (the Kite's, recharged whole) or a vent.

entries.name: At the end of a round it killed in
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as the round ends, after the enemy's turn, for a machine whose own attack killed in that round: once, however many foes fell and however many attacks felled them (the Ammit's flare).

design.holes: Ryan, 16 November, the Ammit's passive in his words: "At the start of the skirmish, or at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy, the Essences Flare, granting 1 Empowered per 5 Essences it holds." A kill is an attack's, as the kill trigger counts it; a machine wrecked in the enemy's turn fires nothing.

entries.name: On a foe killed
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as a death check counts a kill in this machine's fight, whoever or whatever made it, an ally's blow, an Ablate tick and a Mine's blast among them: a status, once for each foe that fell (the Ammit's Essence).

design.holes: Built 12 November for the Ammit's Souls. It fires once for each foe that falls, which is what the trigger is: no effect opts into the count. A foe getting back up, a part and a Bomb's burst are no kill and fire nothing.

entries.name: On damaging a foe
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after a spend of this machine's weapons that took HP off a foe, however many foes it hurt: a status, a shield or a vent. An effect may fire once a round only (the Skua's stack of Ricochet).

design.holes: Built for the Skua's rewrite (Ryan, 11 November: "Damaging an enemy grants it a stack of Ricochet (once per turn)"). The stack lands after the spend that earned it, so none of that spend's shots bounce off it. The once-a-round gate is the effect's own (once: round), open to any effect an event fires.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the machines' dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. A pouch of three: a fourth forces a use or a discard. One comes from a Fracture's pick, and a starting stock chosen in the hangar restocks every battle. It expires when the rift closes.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: Each Fracture of the Rupture meter grants one, unweighted by domain: one of three, a battle-long modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon (an extra reroll a round).

design.holes: Built without one (Ryan, 24 October: maybe not warranted at all); decided after the meter is played, with the economy pass.

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Tier
entries.codex: The hard scaling: a rift's tier is locked as the rift opens and sets the kind of battle: who comes, the sizes of its compositions, the Fractures to the Rupture, how many elites and which, the boss's numbers and escort. The Convergence's tier rises one every four; a rift keeps the tier it opened at, so an old rift never hardens by waiting.

design.holes: Shown on the front's card when the mission map comes; today the campaign runs headless.

entries.name: Ramp
entries.codex: The soft scaling under the tier, never shown: the Convergence as it stands when a battle starts sets how many compositions stand on the field at the start and how thick they are, how fast Rift Pressure fills, how many tears open at a peak and how far the seam creeps. It rises with the run, the same for every open front, and never resets.

design.holes: One table of placeholders (sim/ramp.gd), read by the campaign runner and moved on Ryan's word; the timer's 12 reads as the old clock's number (docs/measurements.md, 30 October).

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex: A cost on a component, printed along its foot as a clock and a number: once spent, its entry goes dark for the rest of the round and sits out that many rounds after it, and the die shows it dark with the clock and the rounds left; the die can still land on it, and nothing in it acts. Rapid's own, the rest of the round, is never printed. No cleanse lifts a cooldown.

design.holes: A price as heat is. Counted after the round of the spend since 12 November (Ryan: "change the count so 1 is how I intended"; the round of the spend counted from 14 October, when a weapon's 1 cost nothing, the die spent for the round anyway). The city's battlefield abilities count their own cooldowns in phases.

entries.name: Gather
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Lorentz Contractor, a debuff): every Mine the field's other foes carry joins the one its target carries, their damage added and their keywords as one.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "moves all mines to a single target, and Exposes that target. The Expose rider will effectively create an AoE expose mine, which we can try and see if it's dangerous." Its Expose is its keyword, so the Mine it gathers carries Expose. A Ward on the target turns the gather away.

entries.name: Detonate
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Syrinx Drone, a weapon): after the spend's own Mine joins its target's, the target's Mine blows now, on it and every foe round its slot.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "Deals a small amount of damage and detonates a foe's combined mine immediately ... The small chip damage makes it add a stack first. Try without a cooldown first." Its chip strike spends a Shock on the target, so a Shock doubles the chip, never the Mine.

entries.name: Regenerates
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Storm Petrel's St. Elmo's Regenerator, a lure): spent on a foe, its own machine gains Regenerating, the stacks it says, a point of shield a stack as each of its turns ends, this one first, and a stack fading then.

design.holes: Self only and never Rapid: the die is its brake (Ryan, 19 October).

entries.name: An ally's action
entries.codex: A rule printed on a buff (the Giant Petrel's Immelmann Booster): spent on an ally whose die is spent, the team pays the rerolls it says, banked or fresh, and the ally's die rolls again, never onto the entry it showed, and it acts again. Spent on its own machine it grants what it says.

design.holes: Its price is the lever if it reads as Rapid embodied in a machine (the bible's Kestrel row); the order is the play, the ally spending first.

entries.name: Rolls its die
entries.codex: A rule printed on a buff (the Giant Petrel's Reheat Uplink): the die of the machine it lands on rolls again, never onto the entry showing. A die already spent rolls nothing.

entries.name: Rerolls a kill
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon (the Giant Petrel's Spindrift Salvo): if its spend kills, the team gains the rerolls it says this round, once however many fell.

entries.name: Grants a reroll
entries.codex: A rule printed on equipment (the Swallowtail's Reveille Horn, the Giant Petrel's Immelmann Booster): spending it gives the team the rerolls it says, at once and past the round's two. While the die is held over its target, the REROLL button lights and shows the count it would leave.

design.holes: The Rallied buff until 15 November (Ryan's mark: "This doesn't need to be a temporary buff or a keyword ... We can communicate by highlighting the reroll button as part of the preview, if one will be granted"; the grant passing the round's two: "allow it"). A reroll the Horn grants still counts toward the Muster when spent on the carrier. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of kit on a machine, and one entry on its die. There is no generic kit: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the machine can do.

design.holes: Multi-slot components were set aside as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

entries.name: Fixed component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis: always on the die, never removed, never sold, and it uses no hardpoint. It is the machine's own: no other machine carries one, and it can never be built.

design.holes: Never bought open. Locked pieces are powerful and unique, never blueprints, so no hardpoint stocks one and none carries a tier (the validator holds it; ContentDB.component_tier answers 0).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

entries.name: Module
entries.codex: Kit inside the machine, not on its die: a few numbers up or down, and at most one rule of its own. A chassis has its module slots (two, three on the Clydesdale), and a module is never spent: it is always working.

design.holes: Fitted in the harness and the quick campaign's hangar: the campaign's roster, the loot that drops them and its hangar wait for the economy pass and the hangar screen.

entries.name: On injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when a blow would destroy a component (a foe's Destroy, any of it on the hull). Effects: no_destroy (the component holds instead of being destroyed).

entries.name: Armour
entries.codex: A chassis number taken off every blow that reaches the hull, flat, never a percentage: a blow on bare hull and what passes a shield alike. A blow at or under the armour does nothing to the hull. Shield is not armoured: a blow on shield costs the shield its full damage.

design.holes: Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Strike order
entries.codex: Foes strike in the order they stand: front rank left to right, then the back rank. Each blow is resolved on its own against the shield standing at that moment, so which foe strikes first decides what a small shield blocks. At first contact the heaviest hitters deploy left.

entries.name: Aim
entries.codex: Whom a foe strikes, picked for every foe on its own as the round opens and shown as its arrow before you act: at random, unless the foe carries an aim. The foes never pile onto a machine their blows would already wreck while another stands. The exposed: weighted toward the machine its blow would hurt most, a shield standing lowering the draw and a shield about to break raising it. Anything: any machine alike. Heat: the hottest machine. The armed: a machine showing an intact weapon or debuff. Fires as one: the rank shares a pick. A move may aim differently from its foe. The pick is a commitment: a foe whose target shields up still swings at it.

design.holes: Content: aim on a foe type and on a move; when on a move is the condition that lets a foe pick it, and a special never fires twice running.

entries.name: Self-Destruct
entries.codex: A blow that spends the striker: after it lands the foe is gone, whole, and nothing brings it back. The blow is the foe's whole life, so it is announced like any other and the answer is to kill it first or to shield what it has picked.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. A self-destructing foe counts as a kill like any other.

entries.name: Every Machine
entries.codex: A blow at every machine: each of its strikes lands on every machine in the fight in turn, so no aim and no lure moves it, and the number shown is what each machine takes. A shield saves only the machine it stands on; the answers that stop the whole blow are aimed at the striker: kill it, suppress it, disrupt it.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. Its number is per machine, so a move with it is priced well under a single blow from the same foe. The name is a working one.

entries.name: Last Act
