entries.codex: A blow a foe lands the moment it falls, shown on it by the skull and its number. It lands at once, before anything else, even when the foe was the last one standing, so shield up before the kill rather than after.

design.holes: Content: on_death.blow, an attack's shape (name, factor, strikes, keywords), beside or instead of a split. The Gargantuan King's Meteor (30 October). A short list of steps since 16 November, on Ryan's mark of 15 November ('foes who, say buff others on death, or debuff on death'): the blow may carry also, and on_death.act is one special in a blow's place with its own also, each an effect a fall may do (Foe.FALL_EFFECTS). No piece carries more than a blow yet, so the codex still says a blow; it and the term's word are his when a carrier lands ('maybe rename to something more interesting').

entries.name: Parts
entries.codex: A foe in parts: a core and the parts that stand with it. While its parts stand (all of them, or any, by the foe) the core is Guarded and takes no damage; a fallen part may grow back after a few rounds; when the core falls, its parts fall with it. Choose what to focus: a part to open the core, or the core to end them all.

design.holes: Content: parts (foe ids), guard (all or any), regrow_parts (rounds). Parts are found by pack and type, one deep, and deploy by the ordinary rules, so beside the core is likely but not placed. The Fallen Weapon's two eyes and the Obsidian Tyrant's rider (30 October); a move may open once a part has fallen (part_fallen).

entries.name: Countdown
entries.codex: A move that gathers before it lands: announced as the round opens, it lands the stated number of rounds later, its warning chip counting down the whole time. Nothing hits while it gathers. Suppress holds it a round, Disrupt breaks it off, and killing the foe ends it.

design.holes: The foe stays on the field while it gathers; its pick holds while the machine stands, and a Lure moves it.

entries.name: Follow-up
entries.codex: A move that names the move its foe announces next round. The first lands, and the second is the next round's intent, so the warning comes a round ahead: Red Capote, then Andalucia. A Suppress on the first, or a Disrupt that turns it, and the second never comes; once announced, the second cannot be Disrupted, only Suppressed.

design.holes: Content: then, on the first move, naming the second (30 October). One deep: a follow-up names none of its own and comes only after the move that names it, never by the roll. A borrowed swing with nothing taken is no follow-up, and the roll decides. Off the player's list since 15 November (Ryan: "I don't think we need to explicitly spell this out for the player. A backend pattern is ok, and it will become obvious through play and mastery by the player"): the engine's pattern, with no term and no row in the list; a move's own readout still says what it names next.

entries.name: Grudge
entries.codex: A blow that grows with the fight: a point heavier for every foe the team has killed this fight, its intent showing the number as it stands. Kill order answers it: the grudge-bearer first, the rest after.

design.holes: The Pilgrim's Karma (30 October), the Tonberry's Everyone's Grudge under a name of ours. Content: per_kill on an attack, the points a kill. Every fall counts but a foe that went whole (a burst, a part falling with its core) and one taken in by a merge.

entries.name: Foe action
entries.codex: A foe has a base attack, the quick read of how hard it hits, and a list of actions: attacks that scale it, and defends, buffs and debuffs it does instead of a blow (bracing against damage, sheltering behind a Barrier, recovering or healing one of its own, regenerating over its next actions, cleansing the team's marks off its own, warding its side against them, readying to get back up, calling up a foe, rallying or priming the others, costing the team a reroll, setting a machine Ablating, purging one, jamming the entry a die shows, scorching or corrupting every machine). A move may do more than one thing, its blow or its special first and then what it does also, and its own text says all of it. Each round every foe on the field picks one by weight before the player acts, so what it will do and to whom is announced exactly. An attack's damage is the base times its factor, and the help text shows the resulting number.

design.holes: A foe's whole brain is its weighted draw and its aim; none plans ahead.

entries.name: Vents all
entries.codex: An attack that fires the machine's whole heat as it is spent: the heat gauge is empty after the shot, and every step of heat fired, the step printed on the entry, adds the component's bonus to the blow before the passives. The shot's own heat cost still lands.

design.holes: Only the first shot of a chain fires the heat.

entries.name: Grows with missing HP
entries.codex: A flat blow that grows with its target's lost HP: it adds its bonus for every step of HP the target is missing, both numbers printed on the entry, read as the die is spent. No roll is involved, so the number is known before the spend, and the die shows it while held over a target.

design.holes: Both numbers are the entry's own (power_per_missing and per_missing), placeholders.

entries.name: Finisher
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: against a foe at half its HP or less its number is doubled, read as the die is spent, so every strike of the spend takes it or none does. The die shows the doubled number while held over such a foe. The Kite's Pinion Driver.

design.holes: A working name. The Coriolis Accelerator's slope as one step (Ryan, 11 November: "is there a way to make the pinion driver simpler but fill the same purpose"); its factor is the entry's own (finisher), a placeholder.

entries.name: Gated
entries.codex: A keyword printed with a condition, such as a Suppress on a foe carrying Brittle or on a foe carrying two Ablating or more: it lands only on a foe that meets the condition, read as the die is spent and before the blow's own riders, so a spend never opens its own gate. Held over a foe where the condition does not hold, the die shows the keyword's chip struck through.

design.holes: Suppress alone carries a gate today. A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: Consumes
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component. A weapon's blow consumes every stack of the status it names on its target and deals a point more for each stack consumed, before the multiplies; the die held over the foe shows the number with the stacks in. Equipment consumes a count its own machine holds, up to the number it prints, and grants a stack for each one consumed (the Ammit's Quintessence Tap and its Essence): the die shows what it would take now, and with nothing to consume it cannot be played.

design.holes: A mine laid from it eats its arrival's stacks. The equipment's form is the Quintessence Tap's (12 November, the Soul Siphon then), the engine's spends and spends_up_to; its text is a session's draft.

entries.name: Ablates its firer
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: spending it sets its own machine Ablating, the stacks it says, after the blow. At the end of the player's turn the machine loses a point of shield a stack, then hull, and a stack fades; a Cleanse takes it off. A price paid in its own shield.

design.holes: A working name for Ryan's name pass. It was fuel for a machine that wanted heat while a machine's Burning was heat; since Ablate (15 November) it is a price alone, the component pass's to read.

entries.name: Ignores armour
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: its blows take nothing off for a foe's armour, its own or Armoured. A Barrier still takes the blow. Written on few pieces, each of a higher tier or behind a gate.

design.holes: Ryan, 15 November, with Breach cut on both sides: "I would remove Breach from the player's side. Ignores armour can be an explicitly written out property"; "the player armour piercing pieces should be higher tier, obviously, or gated, I think. Else they become obvious best faces for certain domains". On the Ammit's Soulcutter Talons, the Wild Boar's next weapon after a Barrier, and the Overclocked Railgun, whose tier is the component pass's. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: The hopper
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon, for a machine with a hopper. One fills it: the loads it prints for each foe its blows damage, after the blow, in place of what the machine's own passive puts in. The other fires it: each load it takes adds its bonus to the blow, up to its most a shot, and the loads it takes are spent, with the Armoured they stood for. The hopper shows under the heat; the die shows what a shot would fire.

design.holes: The numbers are placeholders at the stock pass's scale.

entries.name: Braces
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Breaching Plow's). Spending it Armours its owner, the stacks it says (an armour point each), until its next turn starts: the armour stands behind the blow through the enemy's turn.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it; the stacks are a placeholder.

entries.name: Strikes
entries.codex: An attack's blows per use. A weapon with three strikes lands three separate hits: each lands its own number and carries its own effects, so a rapid-fire weapon procs often; their riders land once all of them have. Against a shield, each strike is its own blow, so once one breaks the shield the next reaches the hull; against armour, every small strike loses the armour, so many small hits are the wrong tool for a heavy target and the right one for a soft one. Foe attacks have strikes too.

design.holes: Heat is paid once per use, not per strike.

entries.name: Static
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Always on. Its effects change a machine's numbers or a component's properties while a condition holds, rather than firing on an event: add_stat and multiply_stat on hull, shield, heat, armour, move or recharge; add_damage_taken and multiply_damage_taken on every incoming blow; set_reach on a component (direct or indirect while a condition holds); suppress, which turns off another effect by id or tag; and the rules a passive writes on its machine's entries, the star on the die: ignore_armour, and spillover (the Overrun Gearing's: damage past a kill in the front rank carries into the foe behind it in the same column, nothing standing behind a massive foe).

design.holes: Every read asks the pipeline; nothing is written to a stat or a component, so an effect that is gone stops answering. A static reach rule cannot be conditioned on reach.

entries.name: Order of operations
entries.codex: Everything that changes a number goes through one pipeline, in one order. Sources: the chassis passive and each fitted component's passive (until refitted), skirmish rewards (until the battle ends), buffs and debuffs (until the skirmish ends, or until the end of a given round). First suppression, shortest-lived source to longest: a live effect that suppresses another by id or tag turns it off, and a suppressed effect suppresses nothing. Then the gate: an effect takes part only if it is live, its trigger fires now, its condition holds, and, for an ability, its component is not destroyed (a destroyed component keeps its stat bonuses and loses its abilities). Then adds, all sources summed; then multiplies, all sources multiplied; then floors and caps; then overrides, where the shortest-lived source wins and the latest granted breaks ties. In an attack, the number (with what fired heat or a target's missing hull adds) comes before the pipeline's adds and multiplies; Nothing is ever stored as a total: every read asks again, so an effect that is gone stops answering. Statuses stack: the same status granted again adds stacks instead of a second copy; an add is worth its value per stack and a multiply is applied once per stack; a status that ticks applies its per-stack tick at its owner's turn, then loses one stack, and is gone at zero.

design.holes: Refit (the hangar) is what changes loadout-scoped effects; not built.

entries.name: Rage
entries.codex: Machine store, the Nemesis's: a foe's hit on its shield banks one, hull damage two (a blow, a bite of its own, an overheat; a blow that breaks its shield and wounds is hull damage), and every blow of its own weapons that a foe's armour or Barrier takes whole two, up to 10, kept for the skirmish. With five banked its Knuckles of Fury go out charged, unasked: they spend the five and are Instant, the die rolling again, a fist included. Never decays; no cleanse or Purge touches it.

design.holes: Capped at 10 (the passive's stack_status cap), spent in fives (the Knuckle's charged price). The numbers are placeholders (Ryan, 11 November: "These numbers are complete randomness anyway").

table.stacks: Yes: one a hit on its shield, two a hull hit or a blow blocked whole, up to 10; five a charged punch
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Hopper
entries.codex: Machine store, the Honey Badger's: every foe its weapons damage puts a load in it (its Chainsaw Claw digs two), up to four, and every two loads held are a stack of Armoured, granted as each round opens and following the loads as they come and go. Its Bullion Fragmenter fires two a shot. Lasts the skirmish; never decays, and no cleanse or Purge touches the loads: a Purge strips the Armoured they granted, until the machine's next turn.

design.holes: Its numbers since 31 October (Ryan's go, then his second fallback on the runner's read the same day): a cap of four, a point of armour for every two loads. What the loads are worth is Armoured, a buff a Purge strips, since 10 November (Ryan: "The buff he gets from it is Armoured, not an ability. Its purgeable, but returns at the start of his turn since its granted by the funnel bar"); the Ore Plate, an ability of its own, before.

table.stacks: Yes: a load a foe its weapons damage (the claw's two), up to 4; two spent a shot
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Scorched
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's scorch: every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe runs 1 hotter per stack, until the end of the player's turn, when every stack goes. Spending a shield, a vent, a buff or a cool weapon plays round it. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: Placeholder numbers.

table.stacks: Yes: its heat a stack
table.lasts: Until the end of the player's turn, every stack at once

entries.name: Overheated
entries.codex: Machine debuff, a stack for every point of heat past the maximum. At the end of the player's turn it burns a point of hull a stack, every turn it stands, and every spend adds to it. The first such turn since the machine's last reboot is its overheat: its shield breaks. Whatever cools takes these stacks first. No Cleanse lifts it; a reboot clears it.

design.holes: The reboot's (Ryan, 13 November: "an uncleanseable debuff on the unit, a stack for every point of heat"), read off the gauge and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write. The hull a stack burns is the trial's OVERHEAT dial, one the game's.

table.stacks: Yes: a point of heat past the maximum each
table.lasts: Until the heat is back under the maximum, or the machine reboots

entries.name: Broken
entries.codex: Machine debuff. A shield at nothing is Broken, whatever took it there: a foe's blow, the overheat, a reboot, or a cost of the machine's own. A Broken shield gains none by any method until its machine reboots. A Barrier is no shield and lands all the same. No Cleanse lifts it.

design.holes: The reboot's (Ryan, 13 November: "the unit cannot gain shield by any method"; "you can break yourself"), a state of the machine and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the machine's reboot brings its shield back

entries.name: Rebooting
entries.codex: Machine status. A machine that has spent nothing this turn may give the turn to a reboot: drag its die onto REBOOT. Its shield drops to nothing at once and it stands bare through the enemy's turn; as the next round opens its heat is nothing, its shield is whole, and Overheated and Broken are gone. It neither burns nor overheats while it reboots. Nothing forces one, and UNDO takes it back like a spend.

design.holes: The reboot (Ryan, 13 November; folded in 15 November), a state of the machine and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Through the enemy's turn, until the next round opens

entries.name: Enraged
entries.codex: Foe status, from a rage (the Goblin Nob's, its own from the fight's start). While the foe stands, every shield, vent or equipment entry the team spends lays a stack on it, and each stack is a point on every blow it lands for the rest of the fight; a weapon feeds nothing. Never spent by a move. Its chip climbs as the stacks do, so the number an intent shows is the number that lands. A Purge lowers the stacks by its number; the rage goes on, so they gather again.

design.holes: The rage's value and the Nob's numbers are placeholders. Permanent for the fight, as built (Ryan, 4 November: "Nob permanent"; Claude's lean, since an elite's job is to make the player change plan). The rage is the foe's own from the start since 8 November: it was a Bellow, the Nob's opening move, so its first round fed nothing (Ryan: "It's not innate? ... That is so unbelievably incorrect").

table.stacks: Yes: the foe's rage a non-weapon spend
table.lasts: The fight; a Purge lowers the stacks, and the rage, the Nob's Ability, goes on

entries.name: Golden
entries.codex: Foe ability, from a golden rage (the Thunder Ape's). Its blows hit its rage's value harder and it wears a point of armour for the rounds its rage says, its chip counting them down with the damage that breaks it. A quarter of its HP lost since it went gold breaks the rage and it staggers: the gold goes and it loses its next action. A Suppress breaks it too; no Purge strips it, an Ability. Calm again, it may go gold again.

design.holes: Monster Hunter's Rajang by archetype, Ryan's read of 4 November (the golden rage "is a mode, not an attack ... a cycle that forces the player into a cycle of attack and defense, broken by a bold player with great timing"). Claude's translation: the window is the decision, shield through its rounds or burst a quarter of its HP through the extra plate to stagger it; the lost action is the bold play's pay, where the swallow's release loses none (the stun row's care; the exit if it reads as a free stun). The add is the move's value and the plate a point; numbers placeholders.

table.stacks: No: one rage at a time
table.lasts: The rage's rounds; a quarter of its HP lost since or a Suppress ends it early

entries.name: Empowered
entries.codex: Foe status, from a rally: it lands on every foe on the field, the rallier too, the moment the rally does, the rally's value in stacks, and every blow the foe lands hits a point harder a stack, an add before the move's factor. It halves as its own turn ends, its action done, rounded down, as a machine's Empowered does at the player's: no move spends it and a Suppress takes none of it. A foe that had acted when the rally landed carries all of it to its next blow; the rallier's own share halves at once. Two rallies add. An intent counts the rallies on their way to it this round.

design.holes: One clock on both sides since 4 November (Ryan: "we try and make it work. If it's unbalanceable, we go back to separate keywords with different clocks"); the next-move clock of 26 October retired. A rally says 2 at the least since 16 November (Ryan: "Buffs and debuffs that decay at end of round should just have a minimum of 2"): one stack halved to none before its rallier's next blow. His exit, for a move several foes may roll at once: "apply 2 if none, otherwise 1".

table.stacks: Yes: each rally's value adds
table.lasts: Halves as its turn ends, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Undying
entries.codex: Foe status, from a Reraise, its own or an ally's. After it falls it gets back up once, whole, in its own slot and at once, unless it self-destructed; it strikes from the next round.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until it falls; it returns once

entries.name: Appropriated
entries.codex: Ability, Gilgamesh's: the number of the piece he holds. His Collect knocks loose the component a machine's die is showing, Jams it through that machine's next turn, and leaves him Appropriated at its number: a weapon's printed blow, and 1 for anything that is no weapon, a fake. His Borrowed Blade lands that number next round and spends it. One piece at a time, what he takes next replacing it. No Purge reaches it; a Ward on the machine turns the taking away.

design.holes: Ryan's mark of 15 November on the steal rider: "Doesn't need to be it's own rider. It grants Jammed on the target, and Gilgamesh gains Appropriated with the value. The ability should be renamed to Collect." Built 16 November as the first move written in steps: a blow that jams, then a step of its own (appropriate). His Ability, a count on his chip that follows what he holds (Ryan, the same day, of the purgeable buff a session had read from "gains": "I think Appropriated is a balance read. Maybe make it his ability, a number that fluctuates depending on what he's currently holding"). The swing is one strike at the piece's number, whatever strikes the piece had, and no keyword of the piece rides it. The steal rider and the foe's own field for what it held left the engine with it. The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: No: its number is the piece's, and what it takes next replaces it
table.lasts: Until its borrowed swing spends it

entries.name: Swallowed
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's swallow. It cannot act, take damage or be targeted: a blow or a move at every machine passes it by, and no ally can shield, vent or buff it. Everything it carries waits: no stack fades, halves or pays, and no timed status runs out, until it is back. It comes back when its rounds run out, the moment its swallower falls, or once its swallower has lost a quarter of its HP since the swallow; let go in the player's turn, it acts that round.

design.holes: Out of play, so everything it carries pauses (Ryan, 16 November: "Swallowed it's out of play so everything should pause"), where a Phased machine's ticks on: its Ablating, Scorched and Sapped wait, its Empowered and Brittle do not halve, its Regenerating pays nothing, it neither cools nor regenerates, a buff of its own holds nothing on the field (Essence Flare), and every timed status on it, a cooldown and a jam among them, moves a round later for each round's end it sits out: the rounds it sat out never came for it. Let go as its swallow's rounds run out, it is back before that round's end is read, the end it was owed from the round it was taken in; let go sooner, it goes on from where it stood. The swallow's own rounds run. It burns nothing while it is out and burns the turn it is back. A session's reads: an event of its fight still reaches it (a foe felled banks an Ammit's Essence), and a reboot it had begun before it was taken still recovers as the next round opens, the second half of a turn already given. Nothing cleanses it.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: The swallow's rounds, or until the swallower falls or loses a quarter of its HP

entries.name: Guarded
entries.codex: Foe ability, a core's. It takes no damage while its parts stand, all of them or any, by the foe, its Ablating and Vitriol included. No Purge touches it.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: While its parts stand

entries.name: Ability
entries.codex: A unit's own mechanic, the rule it plays by: never a buff or a debuff, so no Purge or Cleanse touches it. Its chip shows its mark cut out of a solid tile: the Goblin Nob's Enrage, a core's guard, a Gel's split, a last act, the Thunder Ape's golden rage; the Polar Bear's seal, the Ammit's Essence.

design.holes: Ryan, 8 November, of the Nob's rage: "Nob, and any other enemies with a passive ability, should have an unpurgable passive chip that points out what's going on. Plus, that's how slay the Spire works, where he comes from. It's not a Buff, it's not a Debuff, it's labelled as an Ability, so it doesn't get purged. Can use this for player units as well, like the armadillo's form. Golden rage should be an ability chip too." The tile is a placeholder look, to judge on the phone (RIFTGATE_ABILITY_DEBUG=1).

entries.name: Barrier
entries.codex: Status, on either side. The next blow it takes deals no damage; the blow's riders land. On a machine, the next blow a foe lands on it, until its next turn starts, so a Destroy on that blow finds no hull damage to read; never granted to every ally at once. On a foe, from its own move, the next blow of a weapon the team lands on it, equipment popping nothing, until it pops or its next turn starts.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: A machine's until the next blow a foe lands on it, a foe's until a weapon's blow pops it; either until its next turn starts

entries.name: Ward
entries.codex: Status, on either side; a blow's damage lands. On a machine, no rider a foe lays lands on it this round, from a blow or from a move of its own (ablate, scorch, jam, corrupt, purge), until its next turn starts. On a foe, from a move that wards every foe on the field, no mark the team lays lands on it (Ablating, Brittle, Cryo, Vitriol, Shocked, Exposed, the Web Bomb, the Paradox and the drone), nor a stun, nor a Purge, and a turned mark feeds no Paradox, until its next turn starts.

design.holes: A foe's move that lays a debuff without a blow is a rider too (Ryan, 25 October: "Should stop all riders, even from non-damaging attacks"), so a Stoke, a Stone, an Eruption on every machine and a Diamond Dust all pass a warded machine by. A foe's Ward (28 October) turns the team's marks (Effects.TEAM_MARKS), and since 2 November a stun and a Purge too, on either side, and stands (Ryan: nothing but damage lands on a Warded foe; the exception that let a stun through went with Numbed's roll).

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until its next turn starts

entries.name: Scorch
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Scorched on the machine it hit (Scorch 2: two): every weapon and equipment it aims at a foe runs hotter.

entries.name: Menace
entries.codex: A pack's worth, its threat rating: a lone patrol 1, a heavier patrol 2, a formation 3, an elite or a boss 4, in every domain and at every tier. The Rupture meter, Anathema and salvage count by it. A pack's fall pays it whole. A pack a fight wore down and left standing has paid for the heads it lost, and its fall pays the rest.

design.holes: One weight for the three tallies, flat by tier; salvage's growth by tier and what a boss pays are the economy pass's to set, the boss's four a placeholder.

entries.name: Elite
entries.codex: A unique foe leading its own composition, worth double its menace, emerging at the rift at a Fracture. Each tier names which Fractures bring one; the lead domain's elites come in turn and never twice in a battle, or a wanderer, drawn on the Fracture's roll one time in three and always once the domain's own are spent. An elite stands at the battle's tier as a boss does.

design.holes: Five placeholder kits (the goblin shaman, the Elder Treant, the Leshy, the Old Man of the Desert, the Reaper) for Ryan's marks; the Peak's elite and a Waste hunter wait on them; the Bone Wyvern waits on the slate.

entries.name: Seal
entries.codex: The boss's seal holds until the Rupture: while it does the boss cannot be attacked and joins no fight, its ring inert, SEALED on its readout. The Rupture breaks it, the last Fracture, and nothing else.

design.holes: The seal's look on the ring is a first cut for the phone.

entries.name: Muster
entries.codex: Machine store, the Swallowtail's: a charge its locked pieces spend for their charged forms. Every die that rolls fills it a sliver, about thirty rolls a charge, and a kill by its own guns five rolls' worth; stored up to its cap. Starts each fight empty and never decays; a store, so no Purge touches it. With a charge up, its locked pieces go out charged unasked, unless the charged form has nowhere to land; then the plain form goes out and the charge waits.

design.holes: Every number is a placeholder; carrying it between fights is section 12's heat question.

table.stacks: Yes: a charge about thirty rolls of any die, five rolls' worth a kill by its guns, up to its cap
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Charged
entries.codex: Machine buff. While it lasts the machine's weapons fire with Shock, shown on the die: every foe a fire reaches is Shocked after the blows, a felled one too. A weapon fired spends a stack: a Rapid's second fire is a second fire, a salvo one, a passive's own fire none, and equipment carries it not and spends nothing. A laid shot spends the stack as it is laid and carries the Shock. A Purge lowers it.

design.holes: The Shock primer (Ryan, 2 November), Primed's cousin, so Chain is the arcs alone and the Shock supply is a kit choice; a keyword on the weapon fired, never a mark per hit (3 November: "a multi-hit weapon with Shock would apply it after both hits"), so a strikes gun never cashes what it just laid. No piece grants it yet: capacitor pieces are content to propose.

table.stacks: Yes: a fire spends one
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Supercooled
entries.codex: Machine buff. While it lasts the machine's weapons fire with Cryo 1: a stack a strike on each foe hit, one more than its own on a gun that carries Cryo, shown on the die and laid after the hits, so a fire never cashes its own frost. A weapon fired spends a stack: a Rapid's second fire is a second fire, a salvo one, a passive's own fire none, and equipment carries it not and spends nothing. A laid shot spends the stack as it is laid and carries the frost. A Purge lowers it.

design.holes: The Cryo primer (Ryan, 2 November: "laying 1 cryo at a time makes sense, keeps it a little unique, and avoids massive cooling spikes"; the name his pick), so any gun is a Cryo setter for a turn and the Cryo synergies open past the Cryo Flinger; a stack a strike after the hits (3 November: "resulting in 2 applications, not apply-cash-apply-cash, and not hit-hit-apply once"). No piece grants it yet.

table.stacks: Yes: a fire spends one
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Regenerating
entries.codex: Status, on either side: a point a stack as its turn ends, then a stack fades, so Regenerating 3 gives 3, 2 and 1, the first as the turn it was gained in ends, and a second grant adds its stacks. A foe's, from its own move, is hit points, after its Ablating and Vitriol have ticked, so an Ablate is a race and never a wall. A machine's, from the Storm Petrel's St. Elmo's Regenerator, is shield at the end of the player's turn, after its Ablating and before the foes strike, up to its maximum, and a broken shield takes none though the stack fades.

design.holes: One clock on both sides since 15 November (Ryan: "These are structured as 'Regen 1 per stack' and I'd give all sources either a fixed duration, say 2 or 3 turns, or have it decay one stack at a time"; "Regenerating - agreed"), Ablating's turned round; a value at each of three turns until then. The machine half, the Storm Petrel's, built 30 October, bought by a die entry so a foe's purge takes it. The numbers are placeholders, the foes' unmoved by the new clock.

table.stacks: Yes: a point a stack, grants adding
table.lasts: A stack fades as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Ammo
entries.codex: The Musk Ox's magazine, a bar under its heat bar, a notch an ammo. Its weapons spend ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 2 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1, the price printed where the gun's heat would be; a foe's Scorched still heats them. The magazine holds 10, opens each fight at 3 and gains 1 at the start of every round after the first; a vent the Musk Ox spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2. With too little left, a gun cannot be spent (DRY).

design.holes: Never a buff, so no Purge reaches it. If ammo runs plentiful, the vents' and shields' reloads or the trickle come down.
